description: EMBOSS 6.6.0 entret: the entries of a sequence file (any input format of seqret) are read with the text of every entry stored, and the text of each entry is returned exactly as the file has it (the lines the sequence reader read: the whole alignment for the first sequence of an alignment format, nothing for the later ones). sequenceValue is the USA of the program: a query on the file (file:id, file:acc:value, file:wild*, file{a|b}), a range, a list file or a database defined in definitions (db:id); firstOnly stops after the first entry. The embl, genbank, swiss, gff and the other readers store the lines as the library does (a gff3 entry keeps its version line without the line end). Equals the installed program on 780 runs (every input format, damaged files, queries). A5-8c3h, B09 F257.

sequence.description: The text of the sequence file (any input format of seqret), or a sequence as letters.

sequenceFormat.description: The input format (-sformat); default: the program finds the format.

qualifiers.description: Sequence input qualifiers as typed after the sequence on the command line: -sformat1 F, -sid1 name, -sdbname1 db, -iquery1 query, -ioffset1 bytes, -sbegin1 -send1 -sreverse1 (the range does not change the text of an entry).

files.description: More files by name (file name -> text) that sequenceValue may name: list files, other sequence files, the data files of the databases of definitions.

sequenceValue.description: The USA of the sequence input (-sequence): [format::]file[begin:end:r], file:id, file:field:value, file{a|b}, @list, list::list, asis::TEXT, db:id; the text of sequence is the file 'sequence.dat'.

definitions.description: The text of an EMBOSS configuration file (.embossrc) that defines databases for sequenceValue: DBNAME name [ type: N format: fasta method: direct directory: "dir" filename: "*.fa" ], SET name value.

text.description: The text of the output file: the entries as the readers stored them.

messages.description: What the library printed (warnings and errors).

errors.message: Unable to read sequence ... (no entry matched the query or the file has no sequence)
An input on which the reference program never stops or dies by a fault is refused

examples.name: One entry of a two-entry FASTA file
